title: Finite-rotation elastic solids with exact plane-stress reduction
summary: Saint-Venant–Kirchhoff elasticity through the standard model.step workflow, with objective finite-rotation kinematics, exact plane-stress thickness condensation and consistent tangent.

science.statement: Finite rotations are represented by Green–Lagrange strain, with a linear isotropic relation to second Piola–Kirchhoff stress. Exact elimination of the thickness strain defines the plane-stress energy and tangent.

equations.label: total-Lagrangian elastic potential
equations.expression: \boldsymbol E=\tfrac12(\boldsymbol F^{T}\boldsymbol F-\boldsymbol I),\quad\Psi=\tfrac{\lambda}{2}(\operatorname{tr}\boldsymbol E)^2+\mu\boldsymbol E:\boldsymbol E
equations.description: F is the deformation gradient; E is Green–Lagrange strain; lambda and mu are Lamé constants; energy is per reference volume.

equations.label: plane-stress thickness condensation
equations.description: The eliminated thickness satisfies zero out-of-plane second Piola and Cauchy stresses.

inputs.name: young, poisson, plane_stress
inputs.description: An explicit material choice; nonlinear=True does not automatically change an existing linear material.

outputs.name: energy, stress and tangent
outputs.unit_role: energy per reference volume and stress
outputs.description: S output is Cauchy stress; GREEN is Green–Lagrange strain; P is first Piola; J includes relaxed thickness.

assumptions: Isotropic stateless elasticity, small material strains and finite rotations.
One material with no initial stress or eigenstrain; conservative reference loading.
conventions: 2D forces and energies are per unit reference thickness.
Plane strain fixes F33=1; plane stress eliminates S33 exactly.
Standard finite-strain cell outputs embed this material into three dimensions.
applicability: Elastic cantilevers, imperfect columns and conservative structural stability paths.
limitations: Not a general large-strain rubber model; no near-incompressible mixed formulation.
No automatic dynamics, thermal strains, contact or follower pressure in this release.
Arc-length adapter remains serial; Newton path uses the existing MPI assembly.

usage.minimal_example:
model = models.create(study=studies.static_solid(dimension=2, assumption='plane_stress', nonlinear=True), mesh=domain)
u = model.field(fields.displacement(domain, degree=2))
model.material(constitutive.saint_venant_kirchhoff(young=210000., poisson=.3, plane_stress=True))
model.clamp(u, on=left)
model.traction((-10., 0.), on=right)
result = model.step(target=u).solve_result()

validation_rules: Differentiate energy and stress independently; verify rigid-rotation objectivity.
Compare plane-stress results with three-dimensional homogeneous states.
Reject non-positive J or thickness and restore the accepted state.
Verify load balance, Euler scaling, elastica response and mesh/increment convergence.

references.title: COMSOL: linear elastic material with geometric nonlinearity
Bisshopp and Drucker (1945), Large deflection of cantilever beams
